messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH eviction surge detected in kv-cache pool 'dedicated-01'. eviction_rate > 40% over 5m, p95 latency up ~80ms. Paging @sam @maria :rotating_light:

sam: ack — looking. grabbing dashboard + logs. any customer-facing errors? :eyes:

jen: saw an uptick in tail for embeddings->inference path. not 5xx but request latency p95 up ~120ms for a few tenants. link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/cache-overview

maria: oncall handover note: i'm remote for next 30m then @alex will take after 22:00. i'll try triage then handoff. :wave:

sam: quick checks:
- which pools affected? dedicated-01 primarily, small blips in dedicated-02
- is this eviction storm due to cache size churn or traffic pattern change?

jen: promql I used to spot it:
```
sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total{pool=~"dedicated-.*"}[5m])) by (pool)
/
sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{pool=~"dedicated-.*"}[5m])) by (pool)
```

jen: looks like eviction_ratio spiked to 0.42 on dedicated-01 coincident with a traffic burst from embeddings-heavy jobs.

sam: mitigation proposal — temp measures:
1) increase cache capacity on dedicated-01 by 15% (can do via infra autoscaling override) — reduces churn.
2) apply a temporary alert squelch for noisy eviction alerts for 30m (so on-call can focus).
3) create per-model hit rate panels and add low-hit-rate alert (to catch bad prefixes)

maria: agree. also we should avoid blind full flushes — that would worsen cold-starts.

ops-bot: trigger runbook run: cache_eviction_mitigation

ops-bot: runbook steps executed: scaled pool dedicated-01 +15%, added temporary mute for AlertID: evict-dedicated-01 for 30m.

sam: applied scale +15% — propagation in progress. pinging infra for confirmation.

infra: confirmed instance group resized; new capacity online.

jen: rechecking metrics — eviction_ratio dropping to ~0.12 now, p95 latency recovering.

maria: good. immediate wins done. next actions for post-incident:
- update alert definition to require sustained >25% for 10m before page
- add per-pool and per-model eviction/hit-rate dashboards
- add a synthetic test exercising common prefixes so we get early warning
- create a follow-up ticket INF-4321 for long-term tuning (LRU threshold review + cache sizing guidance)

sam: can we capture noisy signal source? suspected tenant 'music-alpha' had a job that bumped prefix churn.

jen: found a spike in keys with TTL=0 from tenant 'music-alpha' — looks like a config bug that bypasses caching permanence. notifying product.

alex: thanks — forwarding to tenant owner. we'll coordinate a fix and throttle their job if needed.

maria: I'll own the postmortem notes and create the dashboard row. tagging @eng-runtime for kernel-level cache heuristics review.

sam: handoff: i'm good to hand to @alex at 22:00. leaving a direct note in the oncall doc. :thumbsup:

alex: taking over. will monitor overnight and follow up tomorrow morning with a summary.

jen: small PR queued to change alert rule:
```
- alert: CacheEvictionStorm
  expr: increase(kv_cache_evictions_total{pool=~"dedicated-.*"}[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total{pool=~"dedicated-.*"}[10m]) > 0.25
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

maria: also adding a 'squelch-on-blink' temporary flag to our alerting to avoid paging on single-burst spikes; we'll document default to 10m sustain.

sam: thanks team. no customer 5xxs observed but tail latency impacted for a small subset. follow-up ticket INF-4321 for alert tuning + per-model dashboards + tenant throttling plan. closing thread once PR + jira are created.

jen: created PR #789 and dashboard panel. link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/cache-overview?view=per-model

maria: created INF-4321 and assigned to eng-runtime + product. details in the ticket.

ops-bot: Incident resolved: cache eviction rate stabilized, paging squelch expired. :white_check_mark:

sam: closing from oncall POV. will reference INF-4321 in the postmortem.

alex: thanks all. good run. :heart:
